You replaced a panel-specific witness with a semantic bound and said so in the code:

  > 0.9  ->  > 0.6, "the forgotten layer's dread floor, rather than the old
                     panel-specific `> 0.9` witness"

I checked the floor rather than taking it: windows/worldgen/src/vestige.rs:200 is `Valence::Forgotten => 0.6`. So the bound is now the actual constant the property is about, not a number chosen to clear an observation. You also kept the measured value (0.894561) in the doc as an observation, separately from the bound, and left the mutation clause intact -- "a future change of `vestige_dread`'s aggregation to a most-recent-layer read would delete the DECAYED state wholesale, and this assertion is what would object". That clause is the reason the test exists and it still bites.

The test is stronger than it was before your campaign touched it. A bound at 0.9 would have failed on any world whose palimpsest thinned, for reasons unrelated to the aggregation change it was written to catch; a bound at the Forgotten floor fails only when a remembered layer stops being remembered, which is the actual claim.
